description:
The works comprise three modest interventions confined to the ground and lower ground floor rear elevation, all facing onto the applicant's private garden. None are visible from the street. No neighbouring properties have a direct line of sight of any of the works, and so the impact on neighbouring amenity across all three elements is considered negligible to nil (or positive). The works are designed to improve amenity, natural light, thermal performance, and aesthetic quality, whilst remaining sympathetic to the building and the surrounding conservation area, and are respectful to the original Georgian style that has been somewhat lost by prior owners' interventions. 

Kitchen Door

The existing door is a non-original temporary door of thin timber planks in a stable-door style, cannot be locked from the outside, sits in a sunken threshold, and is draughty, thermally inefficient, and out of keeping with the property and area.
The door provides no natural light to the kitchen, a particular issue given the low kitchen ceiling. Replacing it within the existing opening would yield limited improvement, as the outrigger occludes much of the sunlight travelling along the southern aspect of the garden. The opening needs to be widened to capture more light. 
The replacement will be a traditional Crittall-style double door with glass panes, substantially improving natural light, thermal performance, and the connection between kitchen and garden. These replace an incongruous and temporary element with one that is traditional in character.

Outrigger Windows

The outrigger does not appear original to the property and is clearly aging. Its windows are small, single-glazed, and off-centre, with views primarily of the flanking walls rather than the garden. The front window is fixed and fitted with ugly security bars. The side window features inappropriate blue-tinted glazing. Neither provides meaningful light, outlook, or ventilation.
The applicant proposes to convert to a reading room. The front window will span the full width of the garden elevation. The side window will be approximately 50cm wide but of matching height for visual continuity, opening along the vertical axis for ventilation. Both will have timber frames and the security bars will be removed. The works intend to maximise the value of an existing low quality non-original element by enhancing the rear elevation and better integrating the garden and building.

Outrigger Brick Slip Cladding

The outrigger appears non-original and is clearly aging. It is proposed to apply brick slips (brick tiles or brick veneer) to the front and side walls, selected in a light tone to harmonise with the main rear elevation brickwork. In addition to the aesthetic improvement, the cladding will meaningfully enhance the thermal performance of what is currently a cold and poorly insulated room. The brick slips are a thin cladding layer and do not alter the structure or massing of the outrigger.
